subject.title: [Feature]: Discord self-profile updates (strict bot-only scope for nickname/avatar/status)

question: Should OpenClaw add a Discord plugin-owned bot self-profile mutation surface, and if so should it reuse the existing presence action/gate pattern or introduce a distinct `self-profile`/`selfProfile` contract?
rationale: The feature would create a public config/action surface that mutates Discord bot identity through stored credentials, so automation should not choose the authorization, account-routing, validation, audit, naming, or partial-failure contract alone.

options.title: Approve narrow self-profile surface
options.body: Add a Discord-owned, default-off, self-only profile mutation action with explicit account selection, avatar validation, regression tests, docs, and live Discord proof, preferably reusing existing presence/action patterns unless maintainers choose a distinct name.

options.title: Keep presence-only scope
options.body: Leave nickname/avatar mutation out of OpenClaw for now and route status/activity needs through the existing presence action or the open dynamic-presence API discussion.

options.title: Defer identity model
options.body: Wait to design a broader identity model across self-profile, per-binding identity, and webhook/persona delivery before adding Discord bot profile mutation.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow self-profile surface
recommendation.body: Add a Discord-owned, default-off, self-only profile mutation action with explicit account selection, avatar validation, regression tests, docs, and live Discord proof, preferably reusing existing presence/action patterns unless maintainers choose a distinct name.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the closest merged Discord presence work and can route the Discord-specific status/activity boundary with the self-profile decision.
